Kings 219</cite> the Lord <he>מְרַשְּׁלוֹ בהרים</he> breaks it (the force of the wind) through the mountains (v. <cite ref="H01857"><he>חָשַׁל</he></cite>).
Num. R. s. 9, beg. הנואף … מְרַשֵּׁל וכ׳ the adulterer, if one may say so, weakens the power of Deity; a. e.—Part. pass. מְרוּשָּׁל; pl. מְרוּשָּׁלִין hanging down, trailing.

<cite ref="Tosefta Menahot 1:8">Tosef. Men. I, 8</cite> <he>היו מר׳ ומסולקין וכ׳</he> if the priest’s garments are trailing and tucked up (by the girdle), or threadbare &c.; <cite ref="Zevachim 18a:11">Zeb. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>היו מר׳ מסולקין וכ׳</he> if they are too long, or too short, or &c.
<cite ref="Zevachim 18b:2">Ib. 18ᵇ</cite> <he>מר׳ כשרין מסולקין וכ׳</he> if they are too long, they are fit for service, if too short, they are unfit; a. e.

senses.gloss: to be relaxed, weakened. Num. R. l. c. כיון ששמע … נִתְרַשְּׁלוּ ידיו when the artist heard (that the king whose picture he was going to paint was dead), his hands sank down (he was undecided).
units: <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 7:1">Koh. R. to VII, 1</cite> <he>נתגעשו ונתרשלו וכ׳</he> the Israelites were too excited (busy with their own affairs) and too indifferent to attend to Joshua’s burial, v. <cite ref="C01193"><he>גָּעַשׁ</he></cite>. Tanḥ. Sh’laḥ 2 <he>אף … נתרשלו ידם</he> even Moses and Aaron felt themselves powerless; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 16">Num. R. s. 16<sup>2</sup></cite> <he>נתר׳ את ידם</he>. Tanḥ. l. c. <he>אתם … אלא נִתְרַשַּׁלְתֶּם</he> you do not find your hands (you are helpless) and give it up in despair; (Num. l. c. <he>כשלתם</he>); a. fr.
